title: Level 2 project: game inventory

notes: An interface for what every stored thing has, with a default method.
Records for the different kinds of thing.
A checked exception when the store is full; the caller must handle it.
A comparator orders the store: heaviest first, ties by name.
Same shape as the game inventory you're about to build.

exercises.title: Items, rarity and descriptions
exercises.prompt: Rarity (COMMON ×1, RARE ×3, LEGENDARY ×10) is done. In interface Item make the default value() return baseValue() × the rarity's multiplier. Give the records Weapon(name, weight, rarity, baseValue, damage), Potion(name, weight, rarity, baseValue, heal) and Gem(name, weight, rarity, baseValue) compact constructors that call Loot.require(name, weight); write require to throw IllegalArgumentException for a null/blank name or negative weight. Write Loot.describe(Item item) with pattern matching: "Spear (12 dmg, 60 gold)", "Tonic (+25 hp, 15 gold)", and for any other item "Opal (500 gold)".

tests.call: new Weapon("Spear", 4, Rarity.RARE, 20, 12).value()
Loot.describe(new Weapon("Spear", 4, Rarity.RARE, 20, 12))
Loot.describe(new Potion("Tonic", 1, Rarity.COMMON, 15, 25))
Loot.describe(new Gem("Opal", 1, Rarity.LEGENDARY, 50))
new Gem("Opal", 1, Rarity.LEGENDARY, 50).equals(new Gem("Opal", 1, Rarity.LEGENDARY, 50))
tests.name: records compare by value

tests.call: new Gem("  ", 1, Rarity.COMMON, 5)
tests.name: blank name

tests.call: new Weapon("Axe", -2, Rarity.COMMON, 10, 5)
tests.name: negative weight

tests.call: new Potion("Feather", 0, Rarity.COMMON, 1, 1).weight()
tests.name: weight 0 is fine

tests.why: describe should use pattern matching with instanceof (or a switch with type patterns).

hints: default int value() { return baseValue() * rarity().multiplier(); }
Compact constructor in each record: record Gem(...) implements Item { Gem { Loot.require(name, weight); } }
describe: if (item instanceof Weapon w) return w.name() + " (" + w.damage() + " dmg, " + w.value() + " gold)";

exercises.title: The inventory
exercises.prompt: Item, Weapon and Potion are given. Write the checked InventoryFullException(String item, int over) with message "No room for Elixir: 2 kg over". Inventory(int maxWeight) throws IllegalArgumentException if maxWeight <= 0. add(Item) throws InventoryFullException if the total weight would go over the limit (nothing is added). totalWeight(), totalValue(). remove(String name) removes and returns the first item with that name ignoring capitals, or null. Make the comparator BY_VALUE order most valuable first, ties by name A to Z; sortedBy(Comparator<Item> order) returns a sorted copy. Generic method <T extends Item> List<T> ofType(Class<T> type) returns the items of that type in order (type.isInstance / type.cast).

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(10); try { inv.add(new Weapon("Spear", 4, 60, 12)); inv.add(new Potion("Tonic", 1, 15, 25)); inv.add(new Weapon("Axe", 5, 40, 18)); } catch (InventoryFullException e) { return e.getMessage(); } return inv.totalWeight() + " " + inv.totalValue(); }).get()
tests.name: totals

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(10); try { inv.add(new Weapon("Axe", 9, 40, 18)); inv.add(new Potion("Elixir", 3, 90, 50)); return "no error"; } catch (InventoryFullException e) { return e.getMessage() + " / " + inv.totalWeight(); } }).get()
tests.expect: No room for Elixir: 2 kg over / 9
tests.name: full bag

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(50); try { inv.add(new Potion("Tonic", 1, 15, 25)); inv.add(new Weapon("Spear", 4, 60, 12)); inv.add(new Weapon("Axe", 5, 60, 18)); } catch (InventoryFullException e) { return "full"; } java.util.List<String> names = new java.util.ArrayList<>(); for (Item i : inv.sortedBy(Inventory.BY_VALUE)) names.add(i.name()); return names.toString(); }).get()
tests.name: sorted by value, ties by name

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(50); try { inv.add(new Weapon("Spear", 4, 60, 12)); inv.add(new Potion("Tonic", 1, 15, 25)); inv.add(new Weapon("Axe", 5, 40, 18)); } catch (InventoryFullException e) { return "full"; } java.util.List<Weapon> ws = inv.ofType(Weapon.class); return ws.size() + " " + (ws.get(0).damage() + ws.get(1).damage()); }).get()
tests.name: ofType gives typed lists

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(50); try { inv.add(new Potion("Tonic", 1, 15, 25)); inv.add(new Weapon("Spear", 4, 60, 12)); } catch (InventoryFullException e) { return "full"; } Item gone = inv.remove("tonic"); return gone.name() + " " + inv.totalWeight() + " " + inv.remove("rock"); }).get()
tests.name: remove

tests.call: Exception.class.isAssignableFrom(InventoryFullException.class) && !RuntimeException.class.isAssignableFrom(InventoryFullException.class)
tests.name: the exception is checked

tests.call: new Inventory(0)
tests.name: no capacity

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(5); try { inv.add(new Weapon("Club", 5, 10, 4)); } catch (InventoryFullException e) { return "full"; } return inv.totalWeight() + ""; }).get()
tests.name: exactly full is allowed

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Inventory inv = new Inventory(5); return inv.sortedBy(Inventory.BY_VALUE).size() + " " + inv.ofType(Potion.class).size() + " " + inv.totalValue(); }).get()
tests.name: empty inventory

hints: Fields: private final int maxWeight; private final List<Item> items = new ArrayList<>();
add: int after = totalWeight() + item.weight(); if (after > maxWeight) throw new InventoryFullException(item.name(), after - maxWeight);
BY_VALUE = Comparator.comparingInt(Item::value).reversed().thenComparing(Item::name); ofType: for (Item i : items) if (type.isInstance(i)) out.add(type.cast(i));

exercises.title: Test the loot screen
exercises.prompt: The loot screen ranks Loot(name, value) records: most valuable first, equal values by name A to Z; it returns a NEW list and leaves the input unchanged; an empty list gives an empty list. rank() is a correct version. Write static boolean checkRanking(Function<List<Loot>, List<Loot>> ranker): return true only if the ranker follows every part of that rule. We'll hand it rank and several broken rankers. Hint: pass it a mutable ArrayList with a value tie, and check the result AND that your input is unchanged. Treat a crash as a failure.

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(Ranking::rank)
tests.name: the correct ranker passes

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(l -> { java.util.List<Loot> c = new java.util.ArrayList<>(l); c.sort((a, b) -> a.value() != b.value() ? b.value() - a.value() : a.name().compareTo(b.name())); return c; })
tests.name: another correct ranker passes

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(l -> { java.util.List<Loot> c = new java.util.ArrayList<>(l); c.sort(java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(Loot::value)); return c; })
tests.name: bug: cheapest first

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(l -> { java.util.List<Loot> c = new java.util.ArrayList<>(l); c.sort(java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(Loot::value).reversed()); return c; })
tests.name: bug: no tie-breaker
tests.hint_if_fail: Put two items with the same value in Z-A order in your input.

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(l -> { l.sort(java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(Loot::value).reversed().thenComparing(Loot::name)); return l; })
tests.name: bug: sorts the caller's list
tests.hint_if_fail: Keep a copy of your input and check it is the same after calling the ranker.

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(l -> { if (l.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalStateException("empty"); return Ranking.rank(l); })
tests.name: bug: crashes on empty
tests.hint_if_fail: Also try an empty list, and catch exceptions.

tests.call: Ranking.checkRanking(l -> { java.util.List<Loot> c = Ranking.rank(l); if (c.size() > 1) c.remove(c.size() - 1); return c; })
tests.name: bug: loses an item

hints: Build input = new ArrayList<>(List.of(new Loot("Opal", 50), new Loot("Axe", 20), new Loot("Ruby", 50), new Loot("Bow", 20))); and a List<Loot> before = new ArrayList<>(input);
Expected: [Opal 50, Ruby 50, Axe 20, Bow 20]. Compare with expected.equals(result), and before.equals(input) afterwards.
Wrap it all in try { ... } catch (RuntimeException e) { return false; } and also check ranker.apply(new ArrayList<>()).isEmpty().

quiz.q: Why is Item an interface and Weapon/Potion records?
choices: Item is a shared contract; each kind is an unchanging value
quiz.why: Contract in the interface, data in records.

choices: A full bag is a normal situation the game must plan for
quiz.why: Callers are forced to handle it (show a message, drop something).

quiz.q: What does `ofType(Weapon.class)` returning List<Weapon> save the caller?
choices: Casting each item and the risk of a ClassCastException
quiz.why: Generics give a typed list straight away.

quiz.q: Your ranking test input has no two items with the same value. Which bug can slip through?
quiz.why: Ties must be in the test data to test tie-breaking.

quiz.q: Where should the 'no negative weight' rule live?
choices: In every method that uses weight
quiz.why: Then a bad item can never exist.

cards.a: Model the data, then the rules, then the tests.
A compact constructor: record R(...) { R { checks } }

cards.q: What makes a test suite good?
cards.a: It fails for every small bug you can plant: boundaries, ties, empty input, side effects.

explain: Explain how the pieces of your inventory fit together: what is an interface, what is a record, what is an exception, and why each was the right tool.
